item.text: {"summary":"A biennial flowering plant native to Europe, western and central Asia, and north-western Africa, garlic mustard forms low leaf clusters in its first year and flowers the following spring. Its crushed leaves smell of garlic, while its small white flowers are cross-shaped and grow in dense clusters.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"Chopped leaves, especially young ones, flavour salads and sauces; flowers and fruit are sometimes included. Young first-year plants contain cyanide, whose gas is eliminated by chopping.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p2","s1:p3"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p13","s1:p16"]}}
